title: Sitemap.xml
definition: An XML file that lists all the important URLs on a website, acting as a roadmap to guide search engines to all your pages.
simpleExplanation: Imagine a website with 10,000 blog posts. Googlebot arrives at the homepage and has to frantically click every single link it can find to discover all 10,000 posts. A sitemap is a map you hand directly to Google that says: 'Here is a list of every single URL on my site, and the exact date I last updated them.'
realWorldExample: Submitting a sitemap to Google Search Console to guarantee that Google knows your new website exists within hours, instead of waiting weeks for them to organically find it.
useCases: Helping bots discover deeply nested pages

basic: What file format is a sitemap written in?
intermediate: Do you need to write a sitemap manually by hand?

answers.question: Write manually?
answers.answer: Almost never. Frameworks like Next.js, or CMS plugins like Yoast SEO for WordPress, automatically generate the `sitemap.xml` file dynamically every time you publish a new page.

codeExample:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<urlset xmlns="http://www.sitemaps.org/schemas/sitemap/0.9">

  <!-- The Homepage -->
  <url>
    <loc>https://www.example.com/</loc>
    <lastmod>2024-01-01</lastmod>
    <changefreq>daily</changefreq>
    <priority>1.0</priority>
  </url>

  <!-- A Blog Post -->
  <url>
    <loc>https://www.example.com/blog/html-basics</loc>
    <lastmod>2024-05-15</lastmod>
    <changefreq>monthly</changefreq>
    <priority>0.8</priority>
  </url>

</urlset>
